<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אדר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917575_theRebbe_481" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_93_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917575_theRebbe_481__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>There are two aspects within teshuvah itself—middos and mochin—corresponding to the lower and higher forms of teshuvah, which relate to one's existence and self-nullification respectively.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, also in teshuvah itself there are the two aspects of middos and mochin</t>
    <t s="1">(Mishkan Stam and Mishkan HaEidus),</t>
    <t s="2">for teshuvah tata'ah,</t>
    <t s="3">"Tashuv Hashem tata'ah"</t>
    <t s="4">(to the vav),</t>
    <t s="5">is in middos,</t>
    <t s="6">and teshuvah ila'ah,</t>
    <t s="7">"Tashuv Hashem ila'ah"</t>
    <t s="8">(to the yud),</t>
    <t s="9">is in mochin.</t>
    <t s="10">And one can explain this in the context of man's service,</t>
    <t s="11">that teshuvah tata'ah is primarily regarding the service of Torah and mitzvos</t>
    <t s="12">(turn from evil and do good),</t>
    <t s="13">meaning that the leap in teshuvah tata'ah is regarding his existence,</t>
    <t s="14">and therefore it is included in the aspect of middos</t>
    <t s="15">(existence),</t>
    <t s="16">and teshuvah ila'ah is to return his soul to its source as it was united with Him in absolute unity before He breathed it,</t>
    <t s="17">through which he goes out and is nullified from his existence,</t>
    <t s="18">and therefore it is in mochin,</t>
    <t s="19">Binah.</t>
    <t s="20">And based on this,</t>
    <t s="21">the two aspects in the Mishkan are also in teshuvah itself.</t>
    <t s="22">Mishkan Stam is teshuvah tata'ah and Mishkan HaEidus is teshuvah ila'ah.</t>
    <t s="23">And the explanation of the two interpretations of "asher pukad al pi Moshe" can be said,</t>
    <t s="24">that the main aspect of "pukad al pi Moshe"</t>
    <t s="25">(nullification of existence)</t>
    <t s="26">is in teshuvah ila'ah,</t>
    <t s="27">Mishkan HaEidus.</t>
    <t s="28">Nevertheless, this also applies to "Eileh Pekudei HaMishkan,"</t>
    <t s="29">for through teshuvah ila'ah,</t>
    <t s="30">also teshuvah tata'ah is in a more elevated manner.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The explanation of "pekudei" as a term of union is connected to the three aspects of onah, she'erah, and kesutah, and the question arises regarding the connection between Rashi's interpretation of "Mishkan Mishkan" and the interpretation in Likkutei Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this, one can explain what is said in Likkutei Torah on the interpretation of the verse "Eileh Pekudei HaMishkan,"</t>
    <t s="2">that "pekudei" is</t>
    <t s="3">(also)</t>
    <t s="4">from the term pekidah and union,</t>
    <t s="5">like "a man is obligated to be intimate with his wife."</t>
    <t s="6">And it is explained elsewhere</t>
    <t s="7">regarding the matter of she'erah, kesutah, and onah,</t>
    <t s="8">that she'erah</t>
    <t s="9">(food)</t>
    <t s="10">is an influence that is clothed in the receiving vessel,</t>
    <t s="11">kesutah</t>
    <t s="12">(garment)</t>
    <t s="13">is the influence in the aspect of makkif that is above pnimiyus,</t>
    <t s="14">and onah is the influence of the essence that is above even the makkif of the garment.</t>
    <t s="15">And to add,</t>
    <t s="16">that the superiority of onah is not only regarding the influence from above</t>
    <t s="17">(that onah is the influence of the essence)</t>
    <t s="18">but also regarding Yisrael,</t>
    <t s="19">that they receive this influence not through a garment.</t>
    <t s="20">And one can say that this is what Chazal said,</t>
    <t s="21">"One who says... 'I am in my garment and she is in her garment' shall divorce and give the ketubah,"</t>
    <t s="22">that the negation of "I am in my garment" is that the influence from above is without a garment,</t>
    <t s="23">and the negation of "she is in her garment" is that the reception of the revelation is not through a garment.</t>
    <t s="24">And one must understand,</t>
    <t s="25">that this interpretation</t>
    <t s="26">(in Likkutei Torah)</t>
    <t s="27">on "Eileh Pekudei HaMishkan"</t>
    <t s="28">(that "pekudei" is from the term pekidah and union)</t>
    <t s="29">comes in continuation of what is explained there that Mishkan HaEidus is the influence</t>
    <t s="30">(through negative commandments)</t>
    <t s="31">that is above clothing in vessels,</t>
    <t s="32">and "Pekudei HaMishkan" is the influence</t>
    <t s="33">(through positive commandments)</t>
    <t s="34">that is clothed in vessels</t>
    <t s="35">(the aspect of she'erah below, even from the aspect of kesutah),</t>
    <t s="36">and nevertheless it is said of it "Eileh Pekudei HaMishkan" from the term pekidah and union.</t>
    <t s="37">Also, one must understand the connection of Rashi's interpretation that "Mishkan Mishkan" twice is a hint to the Mikdash that was pledged as collateral in two destructions for the sins of Yisrael, with the interpretation in Likkutei Torah that "Mishkan Mishkan" twice are the most elevated influences</t>
    <t s="38">(the influence through positive commandments and the influence through negative commandments),</t>
    <t s="39">and up to "Pekudei HaMishkan,"</t>
    <t s="40">"pekudei" from the term pekidah and union.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Through teshuvah, which comes from the essence of the soul, even the service of Torah and mitzvos transcends limitation, uniting the two aspects of "pekudei" as union and "Mishkan" as collateral.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one can explain this,</t>
    <t s="1">that through the Mishkan which was an atonement for the sin of the Golden Calf,</t>
    <t s="2">it was revealed,</t>
    <t s="3">that the intention</t>
    <t s="4">(from above)</t>
    <t s="5">in the deed of the Golden Calf from the outset was so that through it they would reach the level of teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="6">And likewise regarding the fact that the Mikdash was pledged as collateral twice due to the sins of Yisrael,</t>
    <t s="7">that the intention in this is so that they will reach the level of teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="8">and through this the collateral will later be returned to Yisrael in a more elevated manner than it was before the destruction.</t>
    <t s="9">Now, among the advantages of teshuvah over the service of fulfilling Torah and mitzvos is,</t>
    <t s="10">that the fact that Yisrael does teshuvah even after the separation caused by sins</t>
    <t s="11">("your sins separate")</t>
    <t s="12">is because teshuvah comes from the essence of the soul, which is always connected with the Essence.</t>
    <t s="13">And since the essence of the soul is the "essence"</t>
    <t s="14">(also)</t>
    <t s="15">of the revealed powers,</t>
    <t s="16">therefore,</t>
    <t s="17">through teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="18">also the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos that comes from the revealed powers of the soul is beyond measure and limitation.</t>
    <t s="19">And this is the connection of the two matters in "Eileh Pekudei HaMishkan,"</t>
    <t s="20">"pekudei" from the term pekidah and union,</t>
    <t s="21">and "Mishkan" from the term collateral,</t>
    <t s="22">for through teshuvah that comes from the Mikdash being pledged as collateral, the essence of the soul is revealed,</t>
    <t s="23">and through this also the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos is beyond limitation,</t>
    <t s="24">and even in the manner of "pekudei" from the term pekidah and union,</t>
    <t s="25">Yisrael and the Holy One, blessed be He, are entirely one.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
